<noinclude>
== Usage ==
Two ways to write a word:
<pre>
{{Avatarian|k uh t ah r uh|Katara}}
{{Avatarian|en=katara}}
</pre>

'''By sounds (recommended).''' The first parameter is the word spelled in
'''sounds''' — the same readable codes the translator's "Sounds" box
takes: <code>k uh t ah r uh</code> is ''Katara'' (ARPAbet in CAPITALS and
raw IPA both work too). The second parameter is the English '''label'''.
This draws '''exactly''' the spelling you give, so use it whenever you
know the pronunciation.

'''By English.''' <code>en=</code> hands the English word to the same
'''approximate''' converter the translator uses — good for common words,
rougher on names and loanwords.

Hovering the glyphs shows the label and the IPA, e.g. ''Katara /k ə t ɑ r ə/''.

This template does not draw anything by itself. It just marks the text; a
script loaded from [[MediaWiki:Common.js]] finds every
<code>.avatarian-word</code> span after the page loads and replaces it
with the real glyphs, using the same rendering code as the standalone
translator. With JavaScript off, the plain label (or the sounds, or the
English) is shown instead of a blank.

The sound-code table is in the translator's "How to write sounds" panel,
and in <code>AVATARIAN.md</code> §10 in the project repo.
</noinclude><includeonly>{{#if:{{{en|}}}|<span class="avatarian-word" data-avatarian-en="{{{en}}}">{{{en}}}</span>|<span class="avatarian-word" data-avatarian-sounds="{{{1|}}}" data-avatarian-label="{{{2|}}}">{{{2|{{{1|}}}}}}</span>}}</includeonly>
